input.description: Show package.json and search for callers and fetch usage
Show routes.ts and search for global fetch config

input.reason: I read src/ci.ts and its only caller, src/routes.ts. In src/ci.ts:4, getBuild calls `fetch(`${CI}/builds/${id}`)` with no options argument, so no `signal`, `AbortSignal.timeout` or AbortController is passed. Line 5 then awaits `res.json()` with no bound on how long the body read can take. A search of src/ found no timeout, AbortSignal, undici dispatcher or global fetch override anywhere, and package.json configures nothing that would add one. The only caller is the `build` route handler in src/routes.ts:52 (`body: await getBuild(req.params.id)`). It awaits the call directly, with no race, timeout or try/catch, so a stalled CI response holds that request open until the CI server answers. The finding holds as written, and the Summary is accurate.
input.summary: getBuild CI request has no timeout or abort signal

findings.text: The CI build request has no timeout or abort signal, so a stalled CI response hangs every caller of `getBuild`.
findings.reason: Claim 1, no timeout or abort signal: src/ci.ts:4 calls `fetch(`${CI}/builds/${id}`)` with no init object, so no `signal` is passed. No AbortController, AbortSignal.timeout or global dispatcher timeout is set anywhere in src/ or package.json. Claim 2, a stalled CI response hangs every caller: getBuild awaits both the fetch (line 4) and `res.json()` (line 5) with nothing bounding either wait. Its only caller, the `build` handler at src/routes.ts:52, awaits `getBuild(req.params.id)` directly with no race or timeout, so that request stays pending for as long as the CI response stalls.

input.severity_reason: This is a reliability risk that depends on an outside service. When the CI API stalls, requests to the build route stay open and pile up with no way to fail fast. It doesn't corrupt data or open a security hole, and it only hits the one route that fetches CI builds, not the whole service.
